experiment: E2 who asks first, and delayed choice
a_setup: Alice's plus detector at 3 links and Bob's at 5 (Alice asks first), and the mirror (Bob at 3, Alice at 5, Bob asks first). 1024 fresh registry seeds per setting pair, four setting pairs, lattice outcomes; ask order verified from the registry log.
a_prediction: S = 2.828 within its standard error in both orderings; each of the four E and both plus rates equal between orderings within 3 combined standard errors; Alice asks first in 100% of pairs in the first world and Bob in 100% in the mirror.
a_pass: |S - 2.828125| <= 3 sigma_S in both orderings and every E and rate difference between orderings <= 3 combined sigma
b_setup: Delayed choice. Legal API: no in-world rule can rewrite a detector record's setting on a ray field (field_rules/spatial_interactions are rejected for ray transport), so (i) two worlds differing only in Alice's setting with identical seed and pair number are compared, and (ii) a flagged private-state variant replaces the frozen record in world._nodes between steps: every world is built with Alice at a=0 and Bob at b=8 and the intended settings are written after tick 2 (after emission, before arrival at tick 3) or after tick 3 (the last state before the asking step).
b_prediction: Outcomes depend only on the setting present at the asking tick: the delayed world's outcomes equal, pair by pair, those of the world built with the final settings from the start; CHSH from delayed settings gives S = 2.828 within 3 sigma; changing the setting after the ask (after tick 4) changes nothing.
